abilities.description: Tracks neighboring islands through their shifting shadows and compares their positions against layered historical charts.
abilities.name: Shadow-charting

abilities.description: Can distinguish old ink layers and identify where a chart has been altered or supplemented.
abilities.name: Map restoration

characters.arc: Tamsin begins by secretly comparing the strange new map mark with the Inkwardens' layered charts. When a bridge's tone falters and a crystal brace can only slow its drift, she chooses to share her uncertain findings with the other enclaves rather than present a polished but incomplete map. By the end, she accepts that a trustworthy chart is made through shared acknowledgment, not solitary certainty.
characters.description: A young cartographer raised among the terraced orchards and observatory towers of Aevenreach, Tamsin learned to chart the changing shadows of neighboring islands before she was trusted with the old layered maps. She has ink-stained fingers, a wind-reddened face, and a habit of tucking loose curls beneath a charting scarf. When a fresh mark appears on a map she did not draw, she realizes the failing skybridges may be tied to the histories her own people have kept incomplete.
characters.external_conflict: The spans are wandering as the islands forget their former positions, while the Inkwardens and Crystalwrights disagree over whether to reveal the past or rush repairs.
characters.flaw: She treats every uncertainty as a problem she must solve alone before showing anyone her work.
characters.goal: Assemble an account of the islands' former positions that the rival enclaves can acknowledge together.
characters.internal_conflict: Tamsin fears that admitting what she does not know will make her as unreliable as the disputed maps she hopes to correct.
characters.motivation: Keep the islands connected without letting any enclave decide that another community's history is expendable.
characters.name: Tamsin Vale

abilities.description: Builds and fits braided crystal braces that slow the drift of failing skybridge spans.
abilities.name: Crystal bracing

abilities.description: Reads strain and movement in bridge joints to determine where a brace is most needed.
abilities.name: Structural diagnosis

characters.arc: Oren begins convinced that a sufficiently precise brace is the only honest response to a failing span. When his brace slows the drift but cannot restore the bridge's alignment, he chooses to keep it in place while helping Tamsin test the shared account against the span's changing position. He ends willing to treat engineering as essential support for a communal solution, rather than a substitute for one.
characters.description: A Crystalwright from Cinderwake, Oren designs braided crystal braces for the failing skybridge joints. He is broad-shouldered from hauling equipment across the warm island's glassy vents, keeps his hair cropped short, and wears a belt of carefully labeled crystal fragments. Oren trusts measurements he can repeat and has little patience for ceremonies whose results cannot be tested.
characters.external_conflict: His repairs can slow bridge drift, but the Inkwardens' account of the past is contested and the bridge's missing notes resist a purely mechanical solution.
characters.flaw: He dismisses evidence that cannot be measured immediately, even when it points to a cause his tools cannot fix.
characters.goal: Install a crystal brace on the shifting span toward Cinderwake before its wandering makes passage unsafe.
characters.internal_conflict: Oren wants to believe engineering can protect everyone, but he knows a brace cannot restore an alignment whose shared history has been lost.
characters.motivation: Prevent another island from drifting away while there is still time to brace its bridge.
characters.name: Oren Quill

abilities.description: Recognizes changes and gaps in the notes that support a skybridge.
abilities.name: Tone listening

abilities.description: Guides a group in answering a bridge's notes with the distinct tones associated with their communities.
abilities.name: Chorus keeping

characters.arc: Mira begins demanding an immediate chorus whenever a bridge note falters. When Oren's brace slows the drift but leaves the note missing, she chooses to listen to his measurements and let him finish the repair before asking the communities to answer together. By the end, she can hold urgency and patient listening in balance, inviting discordant voices into the chorus rather than treating them as silence.
characters.description: A Bellkeeper of Morrowmere, Mira tends the tuned bells along the bridge approaches and has spent years learning the island's answering tones. She wears her dark hair in two long braids threaded with small bell ties, and carries a listening rod polished smooth by use. Since the familiar note vanished, she has become more insistent that communities must answer one another rather than simply wait for a repair.
characters.external_conflict: The missing bridge note and the Crystalwrights' urgent repairs leave little time for the shared listening she believes can steady a span.
characters.flaw: She mistakes a moving, imperfect response for a refusal to cooperate.
characters.goal: Bring representatives of the linked islands together to sound and compare their notes along the failing span.
characters.internal_conflict: Mira believes harmony requires every voice, yet fears that listening patiently will cost the islands the time they have left.
characters.motivation: Restore the bridge chorus that once connected the enclaves and keep its silence from becoming ordinary.
characters.name: Mira Reson

abilities.description: Compares arrivals, favors, and route entries to trace discrepancies across the Compact's records.
abilities.name: Route accounting

abilities.description: Brings competing enclave representatives into the same negotiation and keeps discussion moving.
abilities.name: Table setting

characters.arc: Sella begins by offering the old route only as a bargaining chip, convinced that leverage is the only protection the Compact has. When the Bellkeepers explain that the route is needed to reconnect the bridge approaches, she chooses to present the private copy alongside the ledger history that implicates her own circle. By the end, she mediates with an open record rather than a selective one, accepting the loss of control that honest disclosure brings.
characters.description: A Tideledger Compact trader in Liltmarket, Sella manages arrivals, route records, and the guesthouse favors that help rival leaders meet without appearing to concede ground. She wears a weatherproof coat with ledger tabs sewn inside and can spot a changed entry by the shape of its ink. Her family has kept a private copy of an old route, giving her access to a path the other enclaves need and a reason to fear what its disclosure will reveal.
characters.external_conflict: The Bellkeepers need the Compact's old route to restore the bridge chorus, while revealing it may expose who benefited from the earlier revision.
characters.flaw: She uses carefully limited truths to preserve influence, even when withholding details puts others at risk.
characters.goal: Disclose the route that could reconnect the enclaves without letting the Compact bury the history of how it came to possess it.
characters.internal_conflict: Sella wants to be trusted as a mediator but has built her standing on keeping the most consequential route to herself.
characters.motivation: Protect the people who depend on the Compact's routes while preventing its old leverage from becoming another cause of division.
characters.name: Sella Quay

abilities.description: Examines layered charts to distinguish original records from later additions and alterations.
abilities.name: Layer reading

abilities.description: Recalls chart details and records well enough to compare distant entries without relying on a single copy.
abilities.name: Archive memory

characters.arc: Elin begins by letting Tamsin study only the chart layers she considers safe to interpret. When Tamsin's unexplained map mark matches a gap in the founding account, Elin chooses to show the other enclaves the altered record and explain her own omissions. She ends with a more honest stewardship of the archive, accepting that preserving a record means exposing its limits as well as its contents.
characters.description: An Inkwarden archivist from Aevenreach, Elin safeguards the layered charts and preserves the disputed names of the first bridge builders. Her silver-threaded sleeves are often smudged with old ink, and she wears a narrow brass lens for examining fine chart marks. Elin helped teach Tamsin to read the archive, but her own careful habits have kept some of its most troubling gaps unspoken.
characters.external_conflict: The Inkwardens are pressed to reveal a full account while the bridges fail, and the archive contains evidence relevant to the disputed positions and missing note.
characters.flaw: She confuses protecting an archive with protecting people from what it contains.
characters.goal: Help the enclaves compare the founding account and identify what was removed during the Silent Revision.
characters.internal_conflict: Elin wants the past acknowledged, but fears that naming the alteration will destroy the Inkwardens' credibility and her own.
characters.motivation: Keep the record intact without allowing a partial truth to be mistaken for a complete one.
characters.name: Elin Mere

relationships.description: Tamsin Vale and Oren Quill clash over whether the failing spans need an honest shared account before repairs can succeed; his measured fixes challenge her maps, while her evidence exposes the limits of his braces.

Mira Reson and Oren Quill work on the same failing span from different traditions: she listens for its missing note, while he braces its moving joints, and each must make room for the other's evidence.
Sella Quay can give Mira Reson access to the old route needed to reconnect the bridge approaches, but Sella's guarded records make Mira doubt whether the route is being shared freely.
Elin Mere taught Tamsin Vale to read the Inkwardens' layered charts, but Elin's initial reluctance to reveal the archive's gaps strains their trust until she shares the disputed record.
